end.summary:
Explored “unity in diversity” through festivals, food, dress, languages and dance.
Identified shared harvest ideas behind Makar Sankranti, Pongal, Bihu and Lohri, while noting different customs.
Gave examples of regional dress, including phiran and ghagra choli, and described India as a colourful collection.
Suggested respectful classroom rules for food and festival differences; the idea that diversity can divide people was not fully corrected.
Teach-back was not passed.
end.parentNote: Riya practised finding common ideas beneath different festivals and connecting regional examples to “unity in diversity.” They used a medley analogy and suggested a clear respect rule: do not insult anyone’s food and discuss everyone’s festivals. Riya raised a concern that differences may cause conflict; this was explored but not fully corrected by the end. At home, ask them to make a two-column list of “different forms” and “shared value” for three festivals.
